newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares still bullish despite budget blow.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares still bullish despite budget blow.

text.p: Nigerian shares gained on Tuesday despite dealers' cold reception of the 1997 fiscal budget in which the military government failed to privatise state enterprises as widely expected.
The all-share index closed at 7122.11 from Monday's 7122.10 and dealers attributed the marginal gain to the adjustment of PZ Industries shares for a scrip issue.
"Most stocks advanced purely on speculation," said one dealer, adding: "Reaction to the budget was mainly one of disappointment in the delay in the long-awaited privatisation."
Finance minister Anthony Ani said on Monday during a breakdown of the budget that government would not be rushed into selling its state enterprises until more studies were carried on the issue.
Niger Insurance climbed to 3.60 naira, up 10 kobo, on its improved 1996 nine-month net profits.
Tyre makers Dunlop Nigeria added one kobo to close at 7.53 naira despite lower profits in its 1996 third quarter results.
Unipetrol's shares surged to 63.63 kobo, up by 63 kobo. Total gained 50 kobo to 61.50 naira and African Petroleum rose by same margin, to 49.00 naira.
Cadbury continued its lead in the food and beverages sector adding 20 kobo to 22.10 naira.
PZ Industries was the day's biggest loser, shedding 7.14 naira to close at 28.56 naira.
Shares of Afprint and United Nigerian Textiles fell on fears the textiles sector might suffer profit erosion after government said it would remove payment of duties on imported textiles this year.
United Textiles slumped 20 kobo to 6.75 naira while Afprint was down by five kobo to 2.50 naira.
